title: Add prerequisite-cycle analysis and valid course ordering
requirement_status: Scheduling and cycle analysis are planned enhancements, not existing behavior promises.
input: CSCI100 requires CSCI200, and CSCI200 requires CSCI100. Compare with a two-course chain in which CSCI200 requires CSCI100.
expected: The proposed scheduling feature reports that the cycle has no complete valid order. For the ordinary chain, a complete order contains each course once and puts CSCI100 before CSCI200.
actual: The current loader accepts both catalogs. The cycle has zero warnings and zero missing prerequisites because both IDs exist. The current API loads, looks up and lists courses; it does not produce a prerequisite schedule.
explanation: Reference existence and orderability are different properties. Both references in a cycle can exist, while neither course can be completed first. The current alphabetic display must not be described as a computed prerequisite order.
limitation: Accepting a catalog for browsing is not automatically wrong. Justin must decide whether invalid scheduling data remains browseable. A new algorithm is required; no existing scheduling implementation was tested or repaired.
plan: Build prerequisite-to-dependent adjacency lists and indegree counts in the shared core. Use a queue-based topological order. Report failure if not every course is processed, then display the result in Qt.
acceptance: A successful order contains every course exactly once, with each prerequisite before its dependent.
Chains, branches, independent courses, self-cycles and multi-course cycles have explicit examples.
Missing prerequisites and malformed import data cannot silently become a complete valid schedule.
Unprocessed downstream courses are not all mislabeled as cycle members.
Graph work remains in the shared core; Qt presents its result.
prerequisite: Python 3 and g++ with C++20 support. This example executes import behavior only; its proposed scheduling outcomes are explanations, not implemented results.
